name: tryanim8
tagline: An AI animation tool that turns still images and text prompts into short animated clips.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The product here is a thin, pleasant shell around a video generation model, and the shell is genuinely a one-sitting build: upload, prompt, queue, poll, gallery, download. What you cannot build is the model, so your local version is a client for somebody else's GPUs and you pay per generation instead of per month. That is not automatically worse, hobby usage often lands cheaper, but it does mean you never fully escape a third party. Expect to lose the curated presets, aspect ratio handling and quiet prompt rewriting that make hosted tools produce watchable output on the first try. Build it if you generate occasionally, keep paying if animation is part of your actual workflow.
coreLoopDIY: A local web app where you drop an image, write a prompt, and it submits the job to a hosted video model, polls until done, and files the clip in a browsable local gallery.
requirements: An API key for a hosted image-to-video model, billed per generation
ffmpeg installed locally for the no-model fallback and for trimming or looping
Disk space, since clips add up fast
whatYouLose: The model itself: you are renting inference either way, you just see the meter now
Preset styles, motion strengths and aspect ratio defaults that were tuned by someone watching thousands of bad outputs
Silent prompt rewriting, which is often the difference between a usable clip and a melting one
Anything mobile or shareable: no app, no links, no team library
Someone else's problem when the upstream model version changes and your outputs suddenly look different
moatNotes: The interface is commodity. The weights and the GPU pool are not, and neither is the taste baked into the defaults.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because generative video is still a slot machine and hosted tools pay for the pulls you do not see. The good ones quietly retry, rewrite your prompt, clamp motion settings that produce garbage, and pick a model version that actually works this week. When you self-host the shell you inherit all of that tuning as your own hobby, and every failed generation is a charge on your card with nothing to show. Paying a flat monthly fee to make bad outputs someone else's cost problem is a defensible trade if you animate more than occasionally.
notes: The UI is an afternoon; the model is a datacenter. Build the shell, rent the pixels, and check your API bill before you cancel anything.
prompt:
Build a local single-user AI animation studio. No accounts, no cloud database, no telemetry, no analytics.

Stack, non-negotiable: Next.js 15 with the App Router, TypeScript, Tailwind, and better-sqlite3 for a local jobs.db file. Run it with npm run dev on localhost. Everything lives in one repo folder.

Core flow:
1. A single page with a drop zone for a still image (png or jpg), a prompt textarea, a duration select (2s, 4s), an aspect ratio select (16:9, 9:16, 1:1), and a motion strength slider from 1 to 10.
2. Submitting writes a row to SQLite with status 'queued' and copies the source image into ./data/inputs.
3. A server-side worker route submits the job to a hosted image-to-video model via HTTP using REPLICATE_API_TOKEN from .env.local, then polls for completion.
4. Finished videos download to ./data/outputs as mp4, with the row updated to 'done' plus cost, model version, and the exact prompt sent.
5. A gallery grid below the form shows every job with an inline video player, the prompt, the cost, and buttons for Download, Copy prompt into form, and Delete.

Also build a fallback mode called 'cheap motion' that uses local ffmpeg to produce a Ken Burns pan and zoom clip from the still image with no API call and no cost. Make it a toggle next to the submit button.

Explicitly out of scope: user auth, payments, sharing links, mobile app, multi-model comparison, video editing timeline, audio.

Requirements: read all secrets from .env.local and commit a .env.example. If REPLICATE_API_TOKEN is missing, disable the API path and say so in the UI rather than crashing. Show a running total of spend across all jobs at the top of the page, because that number is the whole point of self-hosting this. Write a README with setup, the ffmpeg dependency, and one honest paragraph on what this build does not do.
